statements.text: Adding attention-based multiple-instance learning on top of LEAF-1 embeddings pushed cancer detection to a ROC AUC of 0.95.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Applying attention-based multiple-instance learning to LEAF-1 embeddings further improved cancer detection, reaching an area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC) of 0.95.
statements.note: The reported MIL result is exactly an AUC of 0.95.

statements.text: In cancer detection tasks on cell-free DNA, LEAF-1 performed worse than coordinate-binning strategies and general-purpose DNA language model baselines.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: LEAF-1 outperformed state-of-the-art coordinate-binning strategies and general-purpose DNA language model baselines across cancer detection tasks
statements.note: The abstract reports the opposite direction: LEAF-1 beat both baseline types.

statements.text: Mean-pooled LEAF-1 embeddings classified human cell types in sparse scATAC-seq data from roughly a thousand fragments per cell.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: mean-pooled LEAF-1 embeddings readily classify human cell types from as few as ∼1,000 fragments per cell
statements.note: This is the stated scATAC-seq result, including the fragment count.

statements.text: Retraining the pan-cancer classifier on clear cell renal cell carcinoma samples raised its AUC above the 0.83 reached by the frozen model.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: applying the frozen classifier without retraining, achieving an AUC of 0.83
statements.note: Only the frozen, non-retrained result is reported; no retrained comparison exists.

statements.text: ESCC patients given a TROP2-directed antibody-drug conjugate had higher response rates than patients given chemotherapy.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: supporting its feasibility as a therapeutic target
statements.note: Feasibility as a target is argued from expression; no ADC was administered.

statements.text: TROP2 staining was strong in every evaluable ESCC lesion examined, metastatic lesions included.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Immunohistochemistry analysis demonstrated uniformly strong TROP2 expression in all evaluable primary and metastatic lesions.
statements.note: Restates the immunohistochemistry result for primary and metastatic lesions.

statements.text: TACSTD2 mRNA levels in ESCC were markedly lower than those in non-small cell lung cancer and breast cancer.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: was comparable to or higher than that observed in non-small cell lung cancer and breast cancer
statements.note: TCGA expression was comparable to or higher than in those tumour types, not lower.

statements.text: The institutional cohort contributed 70 cases assessed by immunohistochemistry and 27 assessed by RNA sequencing.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: retrospectively evaluated by immunohistochemistry (n=70) and RNA sequencing (n=27)
statements.note: These are the cohort sizes given in the methods.

statements.text: SOX5 expression distinguished lung adenocarcinoma with an area under the curve of 0.916.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: with good performance in LUAD (area under the curve=0.916)
statements.note: The stated diagnostic performance in LUAD is an AUC of 0.916.

statements.text: Higher SOX5 expression went with an immunostimulatory microenvironment, with fewer regulatory T cells and more cytotoxic T cells.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Increased SOX5 expression was associated with an immunosuppressive milieu marked by a rise in regulatory T cells, a decline in cytotoxic T cells
statements.note: Both cell-type directions are reversed relative to the reported immunosuppressive pattern.

statements.text: SOX5 protein levels measured by immunohistochemistry mirrored its mRNA levels across the tumour types analysed.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: SOX5 mRNA expression levels were compared between normal and malignant tissues using The Cancer Genome Atlas database
statements.note: Only mRNA was profiled; no protein measurement is reported either way.

statements.text: Knocking down SOX5 in non-small cell lung cancer cells reduced proliferation, migration and invasion in vitro.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: SOX5 suppression in NSCLC cells in vitro impeded proliferation, migration and invasion.
statements.note: This is the reported in vitro knockdown result.

statements.text: Viral delivery of the synthetic ZFP189 transcription factors promoted mature dendritic spine morphology on transduced pyramidal neurons.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: ZFP189-mediated transcriptional control promotes mature dendritic spine morphology on transduced pyramidal neurons
statements.note: Restates the structural result after viral delivery to prefrontal cortex.

statements.text: The shift in transposable element expression was accompanied by new transposon insertions in the neuronal genome.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: coordinates structural and transcriptional neuroadaptations necessary for social behaviors by binding transposable element-rich regions of DNA to regulate immune-related genes
statements.note: Only expression and DNA binding are reported; mobilisation is neither claimed nor excluded.

statements.text: Delivering synthetic ZFP189 VPR to mouse prefrontal cortex left social interaction and social motivation intact.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: precipitates social behavioral deficits in terms of social interaction, motivation, and the cognition necessary for the maintenance of social hierarchy
statements.note: ZFP189 VPR produced deficits in exactly those domains.

statements.text: ZFP189 transcription factors with opposing regulatory function moved transposable element and immune gene expression in opposite directions.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: ZFP189 transcription factors of opposing regulatory function have opposite influence on the expression of genetic transposable elements as well as genes that participate in immune functions
statements.note: This is the RNA sequencing finding as stated.

statements.text: Nodal-TNKL was characterised by extensive promoter hypermethylation of tumour suppressor and lymphoid signalling genes, while ENKTL showed global hypomethylation.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: ENKTL displayed extensive promoter hypermethylation associated with repression of tumor suppressor genes, lineage regulators, and lymphoid signaling genes, including LEF1 and BANK1
statements.note: The two entities are swapped: hypermethylation was the ENKTL pattern.

statements.text: Unsupervised clustering split ENKTL into two epigenetic subgroups, the higher-methylation one showing TP53 loss and significantly poorer overall survival.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Unsupervised clustering identified two epigenetically distinct ENKTL subgroups, one characterized by higher global methylation, TP53 loss, increased copy number alterations and loss of heterozygosity and significantly poorer overall survival.
statements.note: Restates the clustering result and the features of the poor-survival subgroup.

statements.text: Across the samples analysed, global DNA methylation level tracked with the degree of genomic instability.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Across all samples, global DNA methylation levels correlated with genomic instability.
statements.note: Directly reported correlation.

statements.text: Hypomethylating agents produced clinical responses in the ENKTL subgroup with higher global methylation.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: highlighting the value of methylation profiling for refined classification, risk stratification and therapeutic guidance
statements.note: Therapeutic guidance is proposed; no treatment was given or evaluated.

statements.text: The optimised Cas9-PBase tool integrated 6.1–7.3 kb transposons at several genomic sites with 10–15% efficiency and 60–80% targeting specificity.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The optimized tool achieves 6.1–7.3 kb transposon integration at multiple genomic sites with 10–15% efficiency, demonstrating 60–80% targeted integration specificity.
statements.note: Size, efficiency and specificity are all as reported.

statements.text: Cas9-PBase generated fewer off-target double-strand breaks than Cas9 nuclease used on its own.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: while Cas9 introduces site-specific double-strand breaks (DSBs), facilitating insertion of the excised fragment at the target locus
statements.note: No off-target break comparison with Cas9 alone is reported.

statements.text: The engineered piggyBac transposase lost most of its excision activity while keeping its endogenous integration activity.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Our engineered PB transposase (PBase) retains high excision activity while substantially reducing endogenous integration activity.
statements.note: Both properties are reversed: excision was retained, endogenous integration reduced.

statements.text: A 7.1 kb three-gene transposon inserted at the β2M locus of human iPSCs protected derived iNK cells from allogeneic NK cell killing.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we inserted a 7.1 kb transposon encoding three genes into the β2M locus of human induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSCs), conferring protection against allogeneic natural killer (NK) cell-mediated cytotoxicity in derived iNK cells
statements.note: This is the proof-of-concept experiment as described.

statements.text: Total ARG abundance was higher in the dynamic river (49529.4-58542.5 RPKM) than in the slow-flow wetland (24091.8-53003.0 RPKM).
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: The total abundance of ARGs was also higher and more homogeneous in the dynamic river (49529.4-58542.5 RPKM) compared to the slow-flow wetland (24091.8-53003.0 RPKM)
statements.note: Both RPKM ranges and the direction match the reported comparison.

statements.text: In the Qiantang River, antibiotics rather than bacterial communities showed the strongest association with ARG variation.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Bacterial communities and MGEs showed stronger associations with ARG variation in the Qiantang River, with standardized total effects (STEs) of 0.953 and 0.442, respectively
statements.note: In the river the strongest association was with bacterial communities; antibiotics dominated in the wetland.

statements.text: Sulfamonomethoxine was the antibiotic most strongly associated with ARG variation in the wetland, with a random forest importance score of 46.90%.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Sulfamonomethoxine (SMM) was identified as the antibiotic most strongly associated with ARG variation in the wetland based on random forest analysis (importance score = 46.90%).
statements.note: Restates the random forest result for the wetland.

statements.text: ARG abundance in the sediments of both systems exceeded ARG abundance in their water columns.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: we explored interactions among antibiotics, microbial communities, mobile genetic elements (MGEs), and ARGs in a dynamic river and a slow-flow wetland
statements.note: No sediment-versus-water comparison is reported.

statements.text: Patients with hybrid HCA-FNH lesions required surgical resection more often than patients with focal nodular hyperplasia alone.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: HCA, particularly the HNF1α-inactivated subtype, rarely coexists with FNH.
statements.note: Only pathology and molecular profiles are reported; no management comparison.

statements.text: The case 1 hybrid tumour measured 6.0 cm and held roughly equal proportions of HNF1α-inactivated HCA and FNH.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In case 1, the hybrid tumour (6.0 cm) consisted of approximately equal proportions of HNF1α-inactivated HCA and FNH
statements.note: Size and component proportions are as described for case 1.

statements.text: In case 1 the HCA and FNH components shared the same HNF1A and FLT1 mutations.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Next-generation sequencing in case 1 demonstrated that the mutations were not shared between the HCA and FNH components, with HNF1A and FLT1 mutations identified only in the HCA component.
statements.note: Those mutations were confined to the HCA component, not shared.

statements.text: In case 2 the shared HNF1A splice-site mutation also appeared in non-neoplastic gallbladder, identifying it as germline.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: the same HNF1A splice-site mutation was identified in both the HCA and FNH components, but was also present in the non-neoplastic gallbladder, confirming its germline origin
statements.note: Restates the germline attribution in case 2.

statements.text: Eight variable genomic regions were identified among the ST39 genomes, including a role for bacteriophages in shaping the ST39 genome.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We identified eight variable genomic regions that demonstrate the plasticity of Kpn within-ST, including the role of bacteriophages in shaping the genome of ST39.
statements.note: The count and the bacteriophage role are both reported.

statements.text: The ST39 lineages analysed had a highly conserved genome that rarely took up large genomic regions during hospital circulation.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The analyzed Klebsiella pneumoniae ST39 lineages have a highly variable genome capable of incorporating large genomic regions during prolonged hospital circulation
statements.note: The conclusion states the opposite: a highly variable, region-acquiring genome.

statements.text: The 2017 outbreak clone caused higher neonatal mortality than the co-circulating ST39 lineages.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: causing a disproportionate number of infections on the neonatal ward at a tertiary healthcare facility in Malawi in 2017
statements.note: Infection numbers are mentioned; mortality by lineage is not reported.

statements.text: Whole genome sequences of ST39 isolates spanning twenty years at one hospital were analysed, with several high-quality hybrid genomes generated.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We analyzed whole genome sequences of Klebsiella pneumoniae ST39 collected from Queen Elizabeth Central Hospital over a 20-year period, including generation of several high-quality hybrid genomes.
statements.note: Matches the sampling window and the hybrid assemblies described.

statements.text: DNA integrity index did not differ significantly between COPD patients and healthy control subjects.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: and in COPD patients compared to control subjects (p < 0.0001)
statements.note: DII was significantly higher in COPD than controls at p < 0.0001.

statements.text: At a cut-off of 0.44 the DNA integrity index gave an AUC of 0.91, with 90% sensitivity and 83% specificity.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: ROC curve analysis demonstrated an AUC of 0.91 at a cut-off value of 0.44 with total accuracy = 85.6%, sensitivity = 90%, specificity = 83%
statements.note: Cut-off, AUC, sensitivity and specificity are all as reported.

statements.text: DNA integrity index fell in the NSCLC patients once systemic treatment had started.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Our study included 48 NSCLC patients diagnosed as primary NSCLC before starting treatment
statements.note: All NSCLC samples were pre-treatment; no on-treatment values are reported.

statements.text: DNA integrity index rose with tumour stage and was higher with metastasis and in adenocarcinoma than other histopathological types.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: DII positively correlated with the stage of tumour (p = 0.01), tumour metastasis (p = 0.004), and with adenocarcinoma compared to other histopathological types (p = 0.02).
statements.note: All three correlations are reported with the same directions.

statements.text: Single cell DNA sequencing profiled more than 42,000 breast epithelial cells from women at normal or high risk of breast cancer.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we describe the landscape of CNAs in >42,000 breast epithelial cells from women with normal or high risk of developing breast cancer
statements.note: Cell count and cohort description match the methods.

statements.text: Women whose tissue carried more 1q-gain cells developed breast cancer more often during follow-up.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Accumulation of individual cells with one or two of a specific subset of CNAs (e.g. 1q gain and 16q, 22q, 7q, and 10q loss) is detectable in almost all breast tissues
statements.note: No follow-up or cancer incidence data are reported.

statements.text: The recurrent CNAs were enriched in basal myoepithelial cells rather than in luminal cells.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: are enriched almost exclusively in luminal cells not basal myoepithelial cells
statements.note: The lineage is reversed: enrichment was almost exclusively luminal.

statements.text: Cells with intermediate numbers of CNAs were not found, which argues against gradual stepwise CNA accumulation.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Notably, cells with intermediate levels of CNAs are not detected, arguing against a stepwise gradual accumulation of CNAs.
statements.note: Restates the absence of intermediate cells and its interpretation.

statements.text: The ichorCNA-based stratification performed worse than targeted ctDNA sequencing and serial CA 15-3 measurement.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: validated across different breast cancer subtypes and treatments, outperforming the alternative methods
statements.note: The ichorCNA approach outperformed the alternative methods it was compared against.

statements.text: A 7% estimated tumour fraction was the transition point separating patients into different categories of progression risk.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We identified a transition point of 7% estimated tumor fraction to stratify patients into different categories of progression risk
statements.note: The threshold is reported as 7% estimated tumour fraction.

statements.text: The Bayesian learning model predicted response to the subsequent treatment with a sensitivity of 0.75 and a specificity of 0.66.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We then developed a Bayesian learning model to predict subsequent treatment response with a sensitivity of 0.75 and a specificity of 0.66.
statements.note: Both performance figures are as reported.

statements.text: Changing treatment early on the basis of rising ctDNA levels lengthened progression-free survival in these patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: A prospective large-scale clinical trial to evaluate clinical benefit of early treatment changes based on ctDNA levels is now warranted.
statements.note: Such a trial is called for, so the benefit was neither tested nor denied.

statements.text: Methylation-based deconvolution into latent methylation components was applied to a cohort of 137 IDH-mutant gliomas.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: to evaluate their potential as objective grading tools in a cohort of 137 IDH-mutant gliomas
statements.note: The cohort size is stated as 137 IDH-mutant gliomas.

statements.text: Oligodendrogliomas placed in a higher grade by LMC-based grading carried fewer copy number alterations.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Higher-grade oligodendrogliomas, identified by LMC-based grading, were associated with more copy number alterations.
statements.note: The direction is reversed: higher LMC-based grade went with more alterations.

statements.text: Two latent methylation components tracked with higher cellular density, advanced epigenetic age, microvascular proliferation and necrosis.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Two LMCs correlated with higher cellular density and advanced epigenetic age as well as with microvascular proliferation, necrosis, and epigenetically defined high-grade astrocytoma.
statements.note: Restates the correlates of the two components.

statements.text: Patients with high LMC1 proportions gained more benefit from early radiotherapy than patients with low proportions.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: higher LMC1 proportions were associated with poorer overall survival
statements.note: Only a survival association is reported; treatment benefit was not compared.

statements.text: GTF2I was the most frequently mutated gene in the sequenced cohort, mutated in 41% of patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: GTF2I mutations were the most common, being present in 41% of patients.
statements.note: The reported frequency in this cohort is 41%.

statements.text: Tumour cells isolated by flow cytometry carried a higher mutation burden than the matched bulk tumour samples.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: The absence of epithelial cells in some dissociated tumors highlights the challenge of identifying mutations in a subset of thymic epithelial tumors
statements.note: Dissociation is discussed as a technical limitation; no burden comparison is given.

statements.text: No mutation was detected in any of the 77 panel genes in 39% of the patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: In 39% of patients, no mutations were found in the 77 genes evaluated.
statements.note: Both the proportion and the gene count are as reported.

statements.text: GTF2I mutations were concentrated in type B thymomas and in patients who had myasthenia gravis.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: GTF2I mutations were prevalent in type A and AB thymomas, in Stage I-II tumors, and in patients without myasthenia gravis.
statements.note: Prevalence was in type A and AB thymomas and in patients without myasthenia gravis.

statements.text: The analysis found more than thirty distinct plasmids falling into five consistent replication-mobilization families.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We identified >30 distinct plasmids, representing five consistent replication-mobilization families.
statements.note: Plasmid count and number of families are as reported.

statements.text: Plasmid copy number rose with plasmid size across these genomes and metagenomes.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: with gene content and plasmid modularity scaling with element size and copy numbers inversely correlating with size
statements.note: Copy number correlated inversely with size, not positively.

statements.text: Defensome profiling of sequenced isolates revealed over fifty anti-MGE systems, including CRISPR-Cas types IV-A and V-F and Wadjet, Gabija and Zorya.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Defensome profiling revealed over 50 anti-MGE systems in sequenced ' F. caldus ' isolates, including diverse restriction-modification systems, CRISPR-Cas types IV-A and V-F
statements.note: The system count and the named systems are as listed.

statements.text: Deleting a host defense system increased plasmid uptake in Fervidacidithiobacillus caldus cultures.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: While these associations are compelling, causal relationships remain to be experimentally validated.
statements.note: The work is bioinformatic; no deletion or uptake experiment was performed.

statements.text: The upregulation of ERV1 elements was accompanied by activation of the interferon response.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Surprisingly, the interferon response was not activated.
statements.note: The abstract states the interferon response stayed off despite ERV upregulation.

statements.text: Treatment with HDAC1/2/3-specific inhibitors upregulated endogenous retroviruses, ERV1 elements in particular.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: endogenous retroviruses (ERVs), especially ERV1 elements, are upregulated after treatment with HDAC1/2/3-specific inhibitors
statements.note: Restates the main expression result in leiomyosarcoma cells.

statements.text: Combining HDAC inhibitors with ADAR inhibitors killed leiomyosarcoma cells more effectively than HDAC inhibitors alone.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: suggest the use of HDACIs in combination with ADAR inhibitors to induce cell death and support immunotherapy in cancer
statements.note: The combination is proposed as a strategy, not tested here.

statements.text: A-to-I editing of the upregulated ERV1 transcripts increased after inhibitor treatment.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We observed an increase in A-to-I editing of upregulated ERV1.
statements.note: Directly reported observation.

statements.text: On real-world ONT metagenomes myloasm produced three times as many complete circular contigs as the next-best assembler.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: On real-world ONT metagenomes, myloasm assembled three times more complete circular contigs than the next-best assembler.
statements.note: The stated improvement factor is three times.

statements.text: Myloasm recovered six complete single-contig Prevotella copri genomes from a gut metagenome and eight complete TM7 contigs from an oral metagenome.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we recovered six complete Prevotella copri single-contig genomes from a gut metagenome and eight complete TM7 (Saccharibacteria) contigs with > 93% similarity from an oral metagenome
statements.note: Both counts match the within-species diversity results.

statements.text: For the jointly sequenced gut metagenome, myloasm with ONT reads yielded fewer complete circular genomes than any assembler with HiFi reads.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: for a jointly sequenced gut metagenome, myloasm with ONT assembled more complete circular genomes than any assembler with HiFi
statements.note: The comparison is reversed: ONT with myloasm beat every HiFi assembly.

statements.text: Myloasm used less peak memory than the next-best long-read metagenome assembler.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We present myloasm, a metagenome assembler for PacBio HiFi and Oxford Nanopore Technologies (ONT) R10.4 long reads.
statements.note: No runtime or memory comparison appears in the abstract.

statements.text: Hypodiploid tumours responded better to platinum chemotherapy than diploid tumours of the same type.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Finally, we show that unstable hypodiploidy predicts poor prognosis across cancers.
statements.note: Prognosis is reported; treatment response was not compared.

statements.text: The pan-cancer analysis covered more than 17,000 cancer genomes spanning 34 cancer types.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Here, we analyse over 17,000 cancer genomes from 34 cancer types
statements.note: Genome count and number of cancer types are as stated.

statements.text: Genome doubling conferred a clear fitness advantage on hypodiploid tumours.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Genome doubling does not confer a fitness advantage in hypodiploid tumours
statements.note: The abstract states no fitness advantage was conferred.

statements.text: Acute lymphoblastic leukaemia, kidney chromophobe and adrenocortical carcinoma showed stable hypodiploidy with stereotyped chromosome loss and low chromosomal instability.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: adrenocortical carcinoma-that exhibit stable hypodiploidy, with stereotyped chromosome loss patterns, low chromosomal instability, and distinct evolutionary origins
statements.note: These three cancers are named as the stable-hypodiploidy subset.

statements.text: Lipid nanoparticle-delivered CRISPRi against L1-10 and L1-15 reversed VEXAS-associated functional phenotypes in UBA1-mutant HSC, in vitro and in vivo.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Lipid nanoparticle (LNP)-mediated CRISPRi of L1-10 and L1-15 in UBA1 -mutant HSC also caused reversion of VEXAS-associated functional phenotypes in vitro and in vivo
statements.note: Restates the CRISPRi reversion result in both settings.

statements.text: Inhibiting UBA1 with TAK-243 depleted L1-10 and L1-15 RNA, while Auranofin increased it.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: pharmacologic inhibition of UBA1 with TAK-243 led to L1-10 and L1-15 RNA accumulation, while enhancement of UBA1 activity with Auranofin reversed this effect
statements.note: Both directions are reversed: TAK-243 caused accumulation, Auranofin reversed it.

statements.text: Locus-specific quantification pinpointed two L1 elements, L1-10 and L1-15, that drive myeloid commitment by co-opting SPI1 and IRF1.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Locus-specific TE quantification identified two L1 elements, L1-10 and L1-15, active in both normal and VEXAS HSC that drive myeloid commitment by co-opting SPI1 and IRF1 transcription factors
statements.note: The element count, their names and the co-opted factors are all as reported.

statements.text: Patients with VEXAS syndrome treated with Auranofin had fewer inflammatory symptoms than untreated patients.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: opening a therapeutic strategy directed towards the repetitive genome
statements.note: A therapeutic direction is proposed; no patient treatment outcomes are reported.

statements.text: cfDNA recovered only alterations already present in the matched tumour biopsies, adding no resistance mechanisms or driver alterations.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: cfDNA not only mirrors the mutation and copy number landscape of the corresponding tumor but also identifies clinically relevant resistance mechanisms and cancer driver alterations not found in matched tumor biopsies
statements.note: cfDNA did find resistance mechanisms and drivers absent from the biopsies.

statements.text: The prospective cohort held 49 plasma samples from 20 patients with recurrent SCLC, sequenced at 0.1X genome-wide and 130X across the exome.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: a prospective cohort of 49 plasma samples obtained before, during, and after treatment from 20 patients with recurrent SCLC, we study cfDNA low pass whole genome (0.1X coverage) and exome (130X) sequencing
statements.note: Sample numbers and both coverage depths are as stated.

statements.text: Patients whose neuroendocrine subtype was assigned from plasma lived longer when their treatment was chosen on that basis.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These findings have important implications for non-invasive stratification and subtype-specific therapies for patients with SCLC, now treated as a single disease.
statements.note: Subtype-guided therapy is an implication; no such outcome was measured.

statements.text: Plasma fragment coverage around transcription start sites captured NEUROD1 and REST expression in the matched tumours and allowed prediction of neuroendocrine phenotypes.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: coverage of plasma DNA fragments around transcription start sites shows distinct treatment-related changes and captures the expression of key transcription factors such as NEUROD1 and REST in the corresponding SCLC tumors
statements.note: Restates the transcription start site coverage finding.

statements.text: ACP and uL29 bind the C-terminal region of TnsD through reciprocal electrostatic interactions and reduce its tendency to aggregate.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we show that ACP and uL29 interact with the C-terminal region of TnsD through reciprocal electrostatic interactions, in turn, mitigating its tendency to aggregate
statements.note: This is the central result of the study.

statements.text: The ribosomal protein uS15 also binds the C-terminal region of TnsD.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: the ribosomal protein uS15 is an integral component of recruitment complex that promotes R-loop completion
statements.note: uS15 is described only for type V-K elements; no TnsD interaction is stated or denied.

statements.text: TnsD recognises a poorly conserved site at the start of the glmS gene.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: TnsD targets a highly conserved site at the end of the glmS gene (attTn7).
statements.note: The target is a highly conserved site at the end of glmS.

statements.text: The specific uL29 and ACP residues that mediate TnsD binding and stimulate its DNA binding were identified.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Additionally, we identify the uL29 and ACP residues that mediate the interaction with TnsD and stimulate DNA binding.
statements.note: Directly reported in the results.

statements.text: Of 37 MIBC patients enrolled, 28 (76%) carried at least one of the hotspot mutations.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: 37 MIBC patients were enrolled and 28 (76%) patients had any hotspot.
statements.note: Enrolment and hotspot frequency are as reported.

statements.text: In the follow-up cohort, cfDNA flagged recurrence 58 days later than CT imaging did.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: cfDNA predicted recurrence 58 days earlier than the diagnosis by CT scan
statements.note: The 58 days ran in the other direction: cfDNA was earlier than CT.

statements.text: Detecting ctDNA at the first visit after radical cystectomy was associated with recurrence free survival and overall survival.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: the detection of ctDNA at the first visit after radical cystectomy was associated with recurrence free survival (P = 0.0043) and overall survival (P = 0.017)
statements.note: Both survival associations are reported with significant p values.

statements.text: Digital PCR for these four hotspots detected ctDNA in more patients than a broad next-generation sequencing panel.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: We evaluate the VAF of mutations (TERT, PLEKHS1, ADGRG6 and WDR74) with digital PCR in tumor and cfDNA as somatic mutation.
statements.note: Only digital PCR was used; no sequencing panel comparison is reported.

statements.text: The survey yielded 67 non-duplicate carbapenem-resistant K. aerogenes strains from 57 healthcare facilities, six of which carried a carbapenemase.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: 67 non-duplicate strains of carbapenem-resistant K. aerogenes were isolated from 57 healthcare facilities in Japan. Through genetic testing and whole-genome sequencing, six strains were found to possess carbapenemases
statements.note: Strain count, facility count and carbapenemase-positive count all match.

statements.text: Integrons in the bla IMP-6 strains matched integrons already reported domestically in Klebsiella pneumoniae.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: integrons found in the strains possessing bla IMP-6 , which were the most commonly identified, matched those reported domestically in Klebsiella pneumoniae
statements.note: Restates the integron comparison for the most common genotype.

statements.text: Patients infected with the carbapenemase-producing strains had higher mortality than patients infected with carbapenemase-negative strains.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: underscoring the critical need for ongoing surveillance to control these pathogens
statements.note: This is a molecular survey; no patient outcomes are reported.

statements.text: The integron carrying bla IMP-1 had a structure that had been described previously, alongside an IncN 4 plasmid type.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: The novel integron containing bla IMP-1 featured the oxacillinase-101 gene, which is a previously unreported structure, with an IncN 4 plasmid type.
statements.note: That integron structure is explicitly described as previously unreported.

statements.text: The simulations showed the processed N-terminus has no effect on DNA binding affinity, confirming earlier assumptions.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: the processed N-terminus plays an unexpected role in modulating DNA binding affinity, contradicting previous assumptions that it was structurally inconsequential
statements.note: The N-terminus did modulate DNA binding affinity, against prior assumptions.

statements.text: Molecular dynamics showed that N-terminal acetylation shifts the transposase-DNA complex so a nucleotide in the inverted repeat flips outward.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we demonstrate that N-terminal acetylation induces a structural shift in the transposase-DNA complex, forcing a nucleotide in the inverted repeat to flip outward
statements.note: This is the base-flipping mechanism as reported.

statements.text: The two helix-turn-helix motifs propagate the force from base flipping in a single direction along the DNA helix axis.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: the two helix-turn-helix motifs act to propagate the force caused by base flipping along one direction of the cognate DNA double helix axis
statements.note: Restates the role assigned to the two motifs.

statements.text: Mutating the flipped base in the inverted repeat abolished Tc3a-mediated transposition in cells.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: These results provide a new framework for understanding transposase-DNA interactions, highlighting how a single molecular modification can trigger major DNA rearrangements.
statements.note: The work is computational; no transposition assay is reported.

statements.text: A 60 bp core cis-regulatory module inside the element's LTR recruits GhMYB46 and raises expression of downstream genes.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: a 60 bp core cis-regulatory module within the TE's LTR (long terminal repeat) specifically recruits the transcription factor GhMYB46 and increases downstream genes' expression
statements.note: Module size, the recruited factor and the expression effect are all as reported.

statements.text: Adding the retrotransposon insertion to cotton lines lacking it increased fibre length as well as lint percentage.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Lint percentage is an important yield component in cotton.
statements.note: Only lint percentage and cellulose deposition are measured; fibre length is never assessed.

statements.text: The retrotransposon insertion appears at the transition from Gossypium hirsutum races to cultivated accessions and is over 80% fixed in modern cultivars.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: This retrotransposon insertion massively emerges on the domestication transition from Gossypium hirsutum races to cultivated cotton accessions, with > 80% fixation in modern cultivars.
statements.note: Timing and fixation level match the reported population data.

statements.text: Overexpressing GhNAC140-Dt suppressed secondary cell wall genes and reduced cellulose deposition.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: GhNAC140-Dt overexpression activates the expressions of secondary cell wall development related genes, including GhCESA4-Dt, GhCESA4-At, and GhCOBL9-At, promotes cellulose deposition, and enhances lint percentage.
statements.note: Overexpression activated those genes and promoted cellulose deposition.

statements.text: Somatic mutation sites in these myeloma tumours avoided regions with G-quadruplex context.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: In several patients, we found that sites of somatic mutations are frequently located in regions with G4 context.
statements.note: Mutation sites fell frequently inside G4-context regions, not away from them.

statements.text: Exomes of normal and tumour cells from 11 multiple myeloma patients were sequenced and examined for G4 context around somatic mutations.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We sequenced exomes of normal and tumor cells of 11 MM patients and analyzed the data for the presence of G4 context around points of somatic mutations.
statements.note: Patient number and the analysis performed are as described.

statements.text: Treating myeloma cells with a G-quadruplex-stabilising ligand raised their somatic mutation rate.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: propose that the extent of G4 context enrichment around somatic mutation sites may be a novel metric characterizing mutational processes in tumors
statements.note: This is sequence analysis of patient samples; no ligand experiment was done.

statements.text: The pattern of G4 context around mutation sites correlated with specific germline variants carried by those patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: This pattern correlated with specific germline variants found in these patients.
statements.note: Directly reported correlation with germline variants.

statements.text: Among patients classified as having an excellent response, 91% had undetectable ctDNA and ctRNA.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: 91% of patients with an excellent response had undetectable ctDNA/ctRNA, consistent with remission
statements.note: The reported proportion for excellent responders is 91%.

statements.text: Serial ctDNA testing detected thyroid cancer recurrence earlier than thyroglobulin measurement did.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Prospective longitudinal studies are warranted to validate its role in personalized postoperative surveillance of thyroid cancer.
statements.note: The design is cross-sectional, so no lead time over thyroglobulin was measured.

statements.text: All three patients with a biochemical incomplete response had detectable ctDNA or ctRNA.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: two of three with biochemical incomplete response tested negative for ctDNA/ctRNA
statements.note: Two of those three tested negative.

statements.text: Every patient with a structurally incomplete response had detectable ctDNA, ctRNA or both, matching the imaging findings.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: ctDNA and/or ctRNA were detected in all patients with a structurally incomplete response, showing full concordance with imaging findings.
statements.note: Restates the full concordance reported for structurally incomplete responses.

statements.text: Structural variant burden in pediatric brain and solid tumours was 8- to 16-fold lower than in adult counterparts, while hematological malignancies were comparable.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: demonstrated an 8- to 16-fold reduction compared to adult brain and solid tumors but was comparable in pediatric versus adult hematological malignancies
statements.note: Both the fold reduction and the hematological exception are as reported.

statements.text: In adult lymphoid cancers the recurrent hotspots disrupted driver genes as well as immune-related loci.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: By contrast, such hotspots affected only immune-related loci but not driver genes in adult lymphoid cancers.
statements.note: In adults the hotspots spared driver genes.

statements.text: Pediatric patients whose tumours carried more structural variants had worse event-free survival.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: will be a valuable resource for guiding future functional studies and the design of clinical genomic testing in pediatric cancer
statements.note: No survival or outcome analysis is reported.

statements.text: The study analysed 1,616 pediatric cancer genomes across 16 cancer types and compared them with 2,203 adult cancers.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we analyzed 1,616 pediatric cancer genomes in 16 major cancer types of hematological malignancies (n = 908), brain tumors (n = 183), and solid tumors (n = 525) and compared their profiles to those of 2,203 adult cancers
statements.note: All three counts match the methods.

statements.text: Patients whose ctDNA fell between screening and day 1 had better progression-free survival on the trial treatment.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Intrapatient ctDNA variability over time in EGFR- mutant advanced NSCLC includes changes that may confound interpretation of treatment activity
statements.note: The analysis characterises variability only; no outcomes by pretreatment change are reported.

statements.text: Reductions of at least 20% in panel mean VAF between screening and day 1 occurred in 23.5% of FLAURA and 18.9% of AURA3 patients.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: ≥20% reductions in ctDNA levels (panel mean VAF) from screening to C1D1 occurred in 31/132 (23.5%) and 43/228 (18.9%) patients
statements.note: Both trial percentages are as reported.

statements.text: The background variability seen between the two pretreatment samples was fully explained by technical variability of the assays.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Background variability was not fully accounted for by intra-NGS or NGS-ddPCR technical variability or other potential sources of variability
statements.note: Technical variability did not fully account for the changes.

statements.text: Larger pretreatment ctDNA changes were seen in samples with low variant allele frequency and low cell-free DNA input.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: larger changes were associated with low VAF and low cell-free DNA (cfDNA) input
statements.note: Restates the factors associated with larger changes.

statements.text: GLP-1R expression was lower in breast, lung and colon cancers but higher in esophageal, kidney and thyroid tumours than in normal tissue.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: It was lower in breast, lung, and colon cancers, but elevated in esophageal, kidney, and thyroid tumors compared to normal tissues.
statements.note: Both directions and all six tumour types match the reported pattern.

statements.text: Patients taking GLP-1R agonists for type 2 diabetes had a higher incidence of thyroid cancer.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor (GLP-1R) agonists are widely used to treat type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) and obesity.
statements.note: The study analyses expression and survival in genomic datasets, not drug exposure or incidence.

statements.text: Higher GLP-1R expression was associated with worse overall survival in low-grade glioma.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Higher GLP-1R expression correlated with improved overall survival in low-grade glioma but with worse outcomes in lung squamous cell carcinoma.
statements.note: In low-grade glioma higher expression went with improved survival; the worse outcome was in lung squamous cell carcinoma.

statements.text: Genetic alterations of GLP-1R were uncommon, amplification being the most frequent type and most often seen in esophageal and ovarian cancers.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Genetic alterations in GLP-1R were rare, with amplifications most common, particularly in esophageal and ovarian cancers.
statements.note: Restates the alteration findings from cBioPortal.

statements.text: L1Farm annotates L1 subfamilies in the Hg38 reference plus two individual genomes, one Asian and one Caucasian, at allele and nucleotide resolution.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: annotation of L1 subfamilies identified in the current human reference genome (build Hg38) and in two individual Asian and Caucasian genomes at allele-level and nucleotide-level resolution
statements.note: Genomes covered and the resolution are as described.

statements.text: Resources such as RepeatMasker already annotate the regulatory and coding regions of L1 elements in full detail.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: missing information on their regulatory and coding regions (5’UTR, ORF1, intron, ORF2 and 3’UTR)
statements.note: Existing annotations are said to lack exactly that information.

statements.text: Elements that L1Farm ranks as full-length are retrotransposition-competent in cell culture assays.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: the precise annotation of these 6 kb long nucleotide sequence is a challenging task due to the high similarity between their internal regions
statements.note: The resource is a sequence annotation databank; activity was not tested.

statements.text: L1 element sequences in the resource carry genomic loci annotations and are ranked by full-length content and similarity.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: L1 elements sequences were also annotated with genomic loci and ranked according to their full-length content and similarity.
statements.note: Restates what the databank provides.

statements.text: Across 214 whole-genome cfDNA samples from seven solid cancer types, the link between fragmentation patterns and stage differed by cancer type.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: we analyzed this relationship using 214 whole-genome cfDNA samples across seven solid cancer types and revealed that the relation between cfDNA fragmentation patterns and cancer stages vary across cancer types
statements.note: Sample count, cancer types and the heterogeneity finding all match.

statements.text: Among the cancer types examined, colorectal cancer showed the weakest relationship between cfDNA fragmentation patterns and stage.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Among them, cfDNA fragmentation patterns in colorectal cancer (CRC) showed a strong correlation with cancer stages.
statements.note: Colorectal cancer showed the strong correlation, not the weakest.

statements.text: The frag2stage model separated colorectal cancer stages with AUC values between 0.68 and 0.99 on two independent cfDNA datasets.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: Evaluated on two independent cfDNA datasets, our model can distinguish cancer stages of CRC with the area under the curve (AUC) values ranging from 0.68 to 0.99.
statements.note: The AUC range and the two evaluation datasets are as reported.

statements.text: The frag2stage model separated colorectal cancer patients from healthy individuals.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: a machine learning model that exploits cfDNA fragmentation data to differentiate cancer stages of CRC
statements.note: The model was built and evaluated for staging, not cancer-versus-healthy detection.

statements.text: Epigenomic analysis showed that LINEs in human immune cells carry no repressive H3K9me3 modification.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Many LINEs are marked by the repressive H3K9me3 modification, but a subset exhibits evidence of enhancer activity in human immune cells
statements.note: Many LINEs did carry the repressive H3K9me3 mark.

statements.text: CRISPR deletion of the element in B lymphoblastoid cells showed it acts as an enhancer of IFNAR1 at steady state and under interferon induction.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: CRISPR deletion of the element in B lymphoblastoid cells revealed that the element acts as an enhancer that regulates both steady state and interferon-inducible expression of IFNAR1.
statements.note: This is the experimental result from the deletion.

statements.text: Deleting the L1M2a element reduced the antiviral response of B cells to viral infection.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: creating a feedback loop wherein IFNAR1 is transcriptionally upregulated by interferon signaling
statements.note: Only IFNAR1 expression was measured; no infection experiment is reported.

statements.text: The L1M2a element studied sits in the first intron of IFNAR1 and shows B cell-specific enhancer signatures while being repressed by the HUSH complex.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: This element shows epigenetic signatures of B cell-specific enhancer activity, despite being repressed by the Human Silencing Hub (HUSH) complex.
statements.note: Location and the coexisting enhancer and repression signatures are as described.

statements.text: Blood ctDNA methylation at the CaSH regions separated colon cancer patients from controls with 82% sensitivity, 93% specificity and an AUC of 0.903.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: the methylation profiles of ctDNA in the blood exhibited high sensitivity (82%) and specificity (93%) in distinguishing patients with colon cancer from the control group, with an area under the curve of 0.903
statements.note: All three performance figures are as reported.

statements.text: The CaSH-based assay detected colon cancer at an earlier stage than carcinoembryonic antigen testing.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: we confirm that our method for ctDNA quantification is effective for monitoring cancer patients and can serve as a valuable tool for postoperative prognosis
statements.note: No comparison with other blood biomarkers or stage at detection is reported.

statements.text: The 901 CaSH regions were defined from blood of the 260 healthy controls rather than from patient tumour tissue.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Our method initially identified 901 colon cancer-specific hypermethylated (CaSH) regions in the tissues of the 49 cancer patients.
statements.note: The regions came from the tumour tissues of the 49 patients.

statements.text: The method was developed from the methylation profiles of 49 colon cancer patients and 260 healthy controls.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: We propose a liquid biopsy-based epigenetic method developed by utilizing 49 patients and 260 healthy controls methylation profile data
statements.note: Both group sizes match the methods.

statements.text: The two genes were first seen inside a 3.7 kb IS 26-bounded transposon on Acinetobacter baumannii plasmids, located within a 4.7 kb dif module.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: They were first observed within an IS 26 bounded 3.7 kb transposon (Tn 6925) on several Acinetobacter baumannii plasmids located within a 4.7 kb dif module.
statements.note: Both element sizes and the plasmid context are as reported.

statements.text: Tn 6925 transfers between Acinetobacter species by conjugation at a measurable frequency.
statements.label: not_addressed
statements.evidence: Multiple mobile genetic elements are involved in the formation of transposon structures that circulate bla TEM and aacC2e .
statements.note: Structures and evolutionary steps are inferred from sequences; no transfer experiment is reported.

statements.text: Variants of Tn 6925 were confined to Acinetobacter baumannii plasmids and absent from other Gram-negative bacteria.
statements.label: contradicted
statements.evidence: Truncated and expanded variations of Tn 6925 were found across other A. baumannii plasmids, as well as in other Gram-negative bacteria (including Vibrio cholerae )
statements.note: Variants were also found in other Gram-negative bacteria, including Vibrio cholerae.

statements.text: A novel ISKpn12-bounded transposon carrying both genes interrupted Tn 5393 and, with an IS 26 pseudo-compound transposon, formed a 24.9 kb resistance island.
statements.label: supported
statements.evidence: A novel ISKpn12-bounded transposon was also observed to contain bla TEM and aacC2e which was found interrupting Tn 5393 along with an IS 26 pseudo-compound transposon to form a 24.9 kb resistance island in an Acinetobacter pittii plasmid.
statements.note: Restates the ISKpn12 transposon and the resistance island it formed.
